title: Optimal Control of Dynamic Gas Networks Using Gaussian Processes with Chance-Constraint Reformulation
summary: Natural gas networks must accommodate variable demand and supply while maintaining pressure across pipelines whose stored gas couples operating decisions through time. Probabilistic surrogates can simplify compressor scheduling, but their predictive uncertainty must remain reliable where optimization uses it. We combine direct learning of the minimum pressure margin with assessment at optimizer-selected schedules.
